# nish/net/tls/client

The client side of a TLS 1.3 handshake (RFC 8446), from its ClientHello to its Finished, carrier-agnostic and sans-IO: the mirror of `nish/net/tls`'s `TlsServer`.

```ts
import {
  TLS_CLIENT_STATE_CONNECTED,
  TLS_CLIENT_STATE_FAILED,
  TLS_CLIENT_STATE_START,
  TLS_CLIENT_STATE_WAIT_AUTH,
  TLS_CLIENT_STATE_WAIT_CERTIFICATE,
  TLS_CLIENT_STATE_WAIT_CERTIFICATE_VERIFY,
  TLS_CLIENT_STATE_WAIT_ENCRYPTED_EXTENSIONS,
  TLS_CLIENT_STATE_WAIT_FINISHED,
  TLS_CLIENT_STATE_WAIT_SERVER_HELLO,
  TlsClient,
  TlsClientConfig,
  tlsClientIsIpLiteral,
} from "nish/net/tls/client";
```

<scalar-code-group>

```ts example.ts
import { TlsClient, TlsClientConfig } from "nish/net/tls/client";

const client = new TlsClient(new TlsClientConfig("example.com", ["h2"]), random, x25519Key, p256Key);
client.start();
// send client.takeOutput(TLS_LEVEL_INITIAL); hand the server's bytes to
// client.receive(level, bytes, 0, n); install secrets as they are known;
// at TLS_CLIENT_STATE_WAIT_AUTH check peerCertificates() and the
// signature, then client.authenticate(ok) (or client.reject(alert)).
```

</scalar-code-group>

<scalar-grid cols="2">

<scalar-card title="tls​Client​Is​Ip​Literal" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#tlsclientisipliteral">

Whether `name` is an IP literal, which RFC 6066 §3 keeps out of `server_name`: dotted decimal (digits and dots only), or anything with a colon, which no DNS name has.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="Tls​Client" icon="phosphor/regular/cube" href="#tlsclient">

The client side of one TLS 1.3 handshake, sans-IO: it takes the server's handshake messages through `receive`, writes its own for `takeOutput`, and derives each secret into `secrets()` as it becomes known.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="Tls​Client​Config" icon="phosphor/regular/cube" href="#tlsclientconfig">

What a client is configured with, the same for every connection.

</scalar-card>

</scalar-grid>

<scalar-callout type="info">

It lives in a module of its own, beside `nish/net/tls` and not re-exported
by it, since Nish has no re-exports; the levels and `TLS_SECRET_*` indices
it shares with the server are `nish/net/tls`'s.

</scalar-callout>

<scalar-detail title="Carrier-agnostic">

As the server does, the client reads and writes
handshake *messages* tagged with their level — the ClientHello and the
ServerHello at Initial, the rest of the server's flight and the client's
Finished at Handshake — and its secrets are readable as they become known.
`nish/net/tls/record-client` puts it on a byte stream.

</scalar-detail>

<scalar-detail title="Sans-IO">

The client random and both private keys, x25519's and P-256's,
are constructor arguments. Nothing here reads a socket, a clock or the
random device.

</scalar-detail>

<scalar-detail title="Authentication is the caller's">

Once the server's CertificateVerify is
read, the client stops at `TLS_CLIENT_STATE_WAIT_AUTH` without looking at
the chain or the signature: `peerCertificates`, `verifyScheme`,
`verifyContent` and `verifySignature` hand them out, and only
`authenticate(true)` goes on to the server's Finished and writes the
client's. A caller that drives this class directly must make that call
itself, after checking the chain against its trust anchors and the
signature over `verifyContent()` under the leaf's key: nothing here does
either, and nothing proves the peer is who `serverName` says until then
(`docs/security/tls.md`, "The client").

</scalar-detail>

<scalar-detail title="What is offered">

TLS 1.3 only, with a 32-byte `legacy_session_id` for
middlebox compatibility (§D.4). The suites, groups and first key share are
the configuration's: by default the three suites this tree negotiates and
the group x25519; `secp256r1` may be configured too, for the first share or
for a HelloRetryRequest to pick. `signature_algorithms` lists ECDSA
P-256 and P-384 and RSA-PSS; `server_name` is sent unless the name is an
IP literal (RFC 6066 §3); ALPN is the configuration's. One
HelloRetryRequest is answered (§4.1.4); resumption, 0-RTT and client
certificates are not here, and a NewSessionTicket is read and dropped.

</scalar-detail>

<scalar-callout type="warning">

**Refusals are alerts.** `receive`, `authenticate` and `reject` answer 0 or
a TLS alert description (`TLS_ALERT_*` in `nish/net/tls/codec`); after one
the client is in `TLS_CLIENT_STATE_FAILED`, every secret it held is wiped,
and it answers the same alert to every call. Nothing the peer sends can
make it panic.

</scalar-callout>

<scalar-detail title="Secrets">

Both private keys are copied into `Secret` fields and the
caller's arrays zeroed; the one the server did not pick is wiped when it
picks, and both once the exchange is done. The ECDHE secret is a `Secret`
wiped on every path; the handshake, traffic and exporter secrets are the
fields of two `TlsSecretPool`s. `fail` and `wipe` zero them all.

</scalar-detail>

The state is a class and a `switch`, with no closures. Written from RFC
8446, RFC 7301 and RFC 6066, not ported from another implementation.

## Functions

### tlsClientIsIpLiteral

Whether `name` is an IP literal, which RFC 6066 §3 keeps out of
`server_name`: dotted decimal (digits and dots only), or anything with a
colon, which no DNS name has.

```ts
function tlsClientIsIpLiteral(
  name: string,
): boolean
```

<scalar-field name="name" type="string" required>

A host name as the caller gave it, such as `TlsClientConfig.serverName`.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="boolean">

True when `name` is non-empty and all digits and dots, or holds a colon anywhere; such a
  name is not sent as `server_name`.

</scalar-field>

## Classes

### TlsClient

The client side of one TLS 1.3 handshake, sans-IO: it takes the server's handshake messages through
`receive`, writes its own for `takeOutput`, and derives each secret into `secrets()` as it becomes
known. It never judges the server's certificate itself: at `TLS_CLIENT_STATE_WAIT_AUTH` it waits for
the caller's `authenticate` or `reject`. One instance serves one connection; once it fails or is
wiped it stays failed.

```ts
class TlsClient
```

| Member | |
| --- | --- |
| `new TlsClient(config: TlsClientConfig, clientRandom: u8[], x25519Private: u8[], p256Private: u8[])` | A client for one connection under `config`, with the 32-byte client random and the 32-byte x25519 and P-256 private keys drawn for it; both keys are copied in and the caller's arrays zeroed. A random or key of another length, or a configuration it cannot offer, leaves the client failed with `internal_error` before it writes anything. |
| `alert: i32` | The alert the client failed with, or 0. |
| `alpnChosen: string` | The ALPN protocol the server chose, one of the configuration's, or empty. |
| `retried: boolean` | Whether a HelloRetryRequest was read, so a second is fatal. |
| `scheme: i32` | The CertificateVerify scheme. |
| `sentServerName: boolean` | Whether `server_name` was sent, so that only then may the server acknowledge it. |
| `sessionId: u8[]` | The legacy_session_id sent, which the ServerHello must echo. |
| `shareGroup: i32` | The group of the key share the last ClientHello carried. |
| `state: i32` | Where the handshake is: one of the `TLS_CLIENT_STATE_*` values, `TLS_CLIENT_STATE_CONNECTED` once it has finished and `TLS_CLIENT_STATE_FAILED` once `alert` is set. |
| `suite: i32` | The negotiated cipher suite, or 0 before the ServerHello (or HelloRetryRequest) is read. |
| `alpn(): string` | The ALPN protocol the server chose, or empty when it chose none. |
| `authenticate(ok: boolean): i32` | The caller's verdict on the server's chain and signature, at `TLS_CLIENT_STATE_WAIT_AUTH`: `true` goes on to the server's Finished, reading what was held meanwhile; `false` is `reject(bad_certificate)`. Answers 0 or the alert; in any other state the client fails with `internal_error`. |
| `peerCertificates(): u8[][]` | The server's DER certificates, leaf first; empty before its Certificate is read. |
| `receive(level: i32, data: u8[], off: i32, len: i32): i32` | Takes the handshake bytes `data[off .. off + len)` the server sent at `level`, a whole message, part of one or several, and reads every message they complete. Answers 0, or the alert the client fails with.<br><br>A level other than the one the state expects is `unexpected_message`, as is a byte left over once a message ends the server's flight at its level (a ServerHello, a HelloRetryRequest or a Finished): RFC 8446 §5.1 forbids a message to straddle a key change. A window outside `data` is `internal_error`. At `TLS_CLIENT_STATE_WAIT_AUTH` the bytes are held until `authenticate`. Once connected, the Application level takes NewSessionTickets, which are checked and dropped; anything else there is `unexpected_message`, KeyUpdate being the record layer's. |
| `reject(alert: i32): i32` | Refuses the server at `TLS_CLIENT_STATE_WAIT_AUTH` with `alert`, the caller's reason (`bad_certificate`, `certificate_expired`, `unknown_ca`, `decrypt_error`…): the client fails with it and answers it. An alert outside 1 to 255 is taken as `bad_certificate`. In any other state the client fails with `internal_error`. |
| `secrets(): TlsSecretPool` | The pool of the negotiated hash: SHA-384's for a SHA-384 suite, SHA-256's otherwise. |
| `start(): i32` | Writes the first ClientHello at the Initial level. Answers 0, or the alert the client failed with; a second call is `internal_error`. |
| `takeOutput(level: i32): u8[]` | The handshake bytes written at `level` since the last call, in a fresh array, and forgets them. |
| `verifyContent(): u8[]` | What the CertificateVerify signature is over (§4.4.3): 64 spaces, the server's context string, a zero byte and the transcript hash. |
| `verifyScheme(): i32` | The CertificateVerify scheme (`TLS_SIGNATURE_*`); 0 before it is read. |
| `verifySignature(): u8[]` | The CertificateVerify signature as sent: DER for ECDSA, raw for RSA-PSS. |
| `wipe(): void` | Wipes every secret the client holds, both private keys and both pools, and fails it: a wiped client has nothing left to go on with. `fail` calls it, and the carriers when a connection ends; wiped without a failure, it answers `internal_error` from then on. |

### TlsClientConfig

What a client is configured with, the same for every connection. The
constructor fills in the defaults; a caller may narrow `suites` or `groups`
or change `shareGroup` before handing it to a `TlsClient`, which checks it.

```ts
class TlsClientConfig
```

| Member | |
| --- | --- |
| `new TlsClientConfig(serverName: string, alpn: string[])` | A configuration for `serverName` offering `alpn`, with every suite this tree negotiates and an x25519 share. Nothing is checked here: `TlsClient`'s constructor checks the whole configuration. |
| `alpn: string[]` | The ALPN protocols offered, most preferred first; empty sends no ALPN. Each is 1 to 255 bytes. |
| `groups: i32[]` | The groups offered in `supported_groups`: a non-empty subset of x25519 and secp256r1. |
| `serverName: string` | The host the client means to reach: sent as `server_name` unless it is an IP literal, and the name the caller authenticates. |
| `shareGroup: i32` | The group of the one key share the first ClientHello carries; one of `groups`. |
| `suites: i32[]` | The cipher suites offered, most preferred first: a non-empty subset of the three this tree negotiates. |

## Constants

<scalar-grid cols="2">

<scalar-card title="7" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`TLS_CLIENT_STATE_CONNECTED: i32`

Both Finished are done and the application secrets known.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="8" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`TLS_CLIENT_STATE_FAILED: i32`

The handshake failed or was wiped: every secret is zeroed, and `alert` says why. No state follows it.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="0" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`TLS_CLIENT_STATE_START: i32`

Built; `start` has not written the ClientHello yet.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="5" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`TLS_CLIENT_STATE_WAIT_AUTH: i32`

The server's chain and signature are read and wait for the caller's
verdict: `authenticate` or `reject`. Bytes that arrive meanwhile are held,
not read.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="3" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`TLS_CLIENT_STATE_WAIT_CERTIFICATE: i32`

EncryptedExtensions is read; the server's Certificate comes next, at the Handshake level. A
CertificateRequest here is `unexpected_message`: this client does not authenticate itself.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="4" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`TLS_CLIENT_STATE_WAIT_CERTIFICATE_VERIFY: i32`

The server's chain is read; its CertificateVerify comes next, at the Handshake level.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="2" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`TLS_CLIENT_STATE_WAIT_ENCRYPTED_EXTENSIONS: i32`

The handshake secrets are known; EncryptedExtensions comes next, at the Handshake level.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="6" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`TLS_CLIENT_STATE_WAIT_FINISHED: i32`

The caller accepted the server; its Finished comes next.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="1" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`TLS_CLIENT_STATE_WAIT_SERVER_HELLO: i32`

The ClientHello is out; a ServerHello or HelloRetryRequest comes next, at the Initial level.

</scalar-card>

</scalar-grid>
